questions.solution: The traditional fighting style of Gatka, used by Nihang Sikh warriors for self-defense and sport, originated in the state of Punjab in India. questions.question: Cricket became an international game with the formation of the _______ in 1909.
questions.questionHtml: Cricket became an international game with the formation of the _______ in 1909.
questions.solution: Cricket became an international game with the formation of the International Cricket Council (ICC) in 1909. The ICC, originally known as the Imperial Cricket Conference, is the global governing body for cricket, responsible for organizing major international tournaments like the Cricket World Cup. It was renamed the International Cricket Conference in 1965 and took its current name in 1989. The ICC, headquartered in Dubai, oversees Test matches, ODIs, and T20Is, along with playing conditions, code of conduct, and anti-corruption measures.

questions.question: What is the penalty for a wide ball in cricket?
questions.questionHtml: What is the penalty for a wide ball in cricket?
questions.solution: In cricket, a wide ball results in the batting team being awarded one run. This occurs when the umpire deems the delivery too wide or high for the batsman to hit with a normal cricket shot. An extra delivery is bowled to compensate for the wide ball, maintaining fairness and the challenge for the bowler. The Laws of Cricket, upheld by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), specify wide ball rules in Law 22.

questions.question: Certain fielding restrictions in cricket during few overs are known as _________.
questions.questionHtml: Certain fielding restrictions in cricket during few overs are known as _________.
questions.solution: The term "Power Play" in cricket refers to fielding restrictions during specific overs to balance bat and ball dynamics. In ODIs, the first 10 overs are power plays with only two fielders outside the 30-yard circle. In T20s, this period lasts for the first 6 overs. These restrictions prevent overly defensive field placements and encourage aggressive batting, while giving bowlers opportunities to take wickets. The 30-yard circle is crucial for enforcing these rules. Power plays are essential in both ODIs and T20s, ensuring a balanced and exciting game.

questions.question: What is the duration of a football match (in regular time)?
questions.questionHtml: What is the duration of a football match (in regular time)?
questions.solution: A football match lasts for 90 minutes, with two halves of 45 minutes each and a 15-minute break. The duration can be reduced only if agreed upon by the referee and both teams. If a penalty kick is taken, the half is extended. A team must have at least 7 players and a maximum of 11, including 1 goalkeeper. An abandoned match is replayed, unless otherwise determined by competition rules or organizers. Option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: When did India host the Asian Games for the first time?
questions.questionHtml: When did India host the Asian Games for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1951.

Key Points

  • The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India in 1951.
  • The event marked the beginning of a major continental multi-sport event for athletes from across Asia.
  • It was the first time India hosted such a large-scale sports event, setting a precedent for future games.
  • The Asian Games are held every four years, bringing together athletes from all over Asia to compete in various sports.

Additional Information

  • Asian Games
    • The Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia.
    • The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi, India, from March 4 to March 11, 1951.
    • The event was organized by the Asian Games Federation until 1978, after which the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) took over the organization.
    • The Asian Games are recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and are the second-largest multi-sport event after the Olympics.
  • Olympic Council of Asia (OCA)
    • The OCA is a governing body of sports in Asia, responsible for organizing the Asian Games and other regional games.
    • It was established in 1982 and is headquartered in Kuwait City, Kuwait.
    • The OCA aims to promote the Olympic movement and sports activities in Asia.
    • The council also oversees the development and progress of sports across the continent.
  • New Delhi
    • New Delhi is the capital city of India and one of its largest metropolitan areas.
    • It has been the host city for many international events, including the first Asian Games in 1951.
    • New Delhi is known for its rich history, cultural heritage, and as a political and administrative center.
    • The city has several sports complexes and stadiums that have hosted various national and international sports events.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers best describes the number of white pieces used in chess?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following numbers best describes the number of white pieces used in chess?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 16.

  • In chess, each player starts with 16 pieces.
  • The 16 pieces for each side include: 1 King, 1 Queen, 2 Rooks, 2 Knights, 2 Bishops, and 8 Pawns.
  • White and Black both have identical sets of pieces at the start of the game.
  • The objective of chess is to checkmate the opponent's King while strategically using all pieces.
  • King:
    • The King is the most important piece, but it is not very powerful. It can only move one square in any direction.
    • The game ends when the King is checkmated.
  • Queen:
    • The Queen is the most powerful piece. It can move any number of squares in any direction.
  • Rook:
    • The Rook can move any number of squares along a row or column.
  • Bishop:
    • The Bishop moves diagonally any number of squares.
  • Knight:
    • The Knight moves in an L-shape: two squares in one direction and then one square perpendicular.
    • Knights are the only pieces that can jump over other pieces.
  • Pawn:
    • Pawns move forward one square, but capture diagonally.
    • Pawns have the option to move two squares forward on their first move.
    • If a pawn reaches the opposite end of the board, it can be promoted to any other piece (except a King).

questions.question: Knockdown and knockout words are related to which sport?
questions.questionHtml: Knockdown and knockout words are related to which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Boxing.

  • Knockdown and Knock out are the terminology of boxing.
  • Knockdown
    • A knockdown happens when a boxer tumbles to the ground of the boxing ring as a result of a blow from the rival. The boxer has to have at least one part of his body other than his feet on the ground for it to be considered a knockdown.
  • Knock Out (KO)
    • A knockout is an automatic win for the opponent.
    • It refers to a player being knocked down for more than 10 seconds. The referee will start counting down from 10 once a player has been knocked down, and the player has to regain his position in order to continue the round.
